  • Strong spreadsheet skills (Google Sheets / Excel — pivot tables, reconciliations).
  • Experience performing bank reconciliations and AR sub-ledger reconciliations.
  • Comfortable authoring and executing UAT test scripts for finance systems and tracking system defects.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and customer service skills; strong attention to detail and a controls mindset.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work across global teams.

  • Exposure to payment gateway integrations and billing middleware (Celigo, iPaaS) or automation tools.

About the Role

Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies. 

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our core team and perform a healthy mix of design and implementation tasks to advance the technical foundation behind the Fivetran product offering.

This team is tasked with evolving a high performance extract-load-trans form data integration system that enables our engineering teams to correctly implement hundreds of data connectors with minimal maintenance effort. The role will challenge you to reason about relational semantics, powerful abstractions, data representation, and software performance. You don’t need to be a subject matter expert before you join us (you will be one before you leave!), but you will need to have experience working carefully with a high impact software team — especially in environments where the best option may not be obvious, your decisions have cascading implications, and where you sometimes need to measure twice before you cut once. A successful candidate will be humble enough to collect diverse input and build consensus, will be experienced and confident enough to be decisive when it’s needed, and will be practical enough to build and iterate on the system while it’s in production. We are also looking for expertise and productivity with both modern and legacy software development environments.

This is a full-time position based out of our Novi Sad office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration.

Technologies You’ll Use

  • C (our main language), Python (used in testing), relational databases (Postgres, Oracle, SQL Server), make
  • GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Jenkins, GCP , Azure, AWS
  • macOS/Linux/Unix/Windows, git

What You’ll Do

  • Learn deeply about Fivetran in order to focus development on practical and relevant system improvements
  • Contribute to the development and planning of our roadmap
  • Collaborate with a small but mighty core team, and with a broader set of stakeholders
  • Work across the project lifecycle: requirements, design, prototype, implementation, review, release, monitoring
  • Review and approve pull requests
  • Care and feel ownership of our product, and leverage your skills towards improving it

Skills We’re Looking For

  • You are execution-oriented, and understand the need to target your “innovation budget” for the greatest impact: you find the middle ground between “perfect, but takes forever to code” and “fixes it now, but nobody will ever be able to understand what I did”
  • You know how to design and code systems and software that is effective, intuitive, easy-to-operate, and elegantly simple
  • You have worked with the relevant tooling and techniques: cloud services, network protocols, serialization, relational databases, etc.
  • You have knowledge of complex structures, object orientation, exceptions, memory management techniques.

Bonus Skills​

  • Experience with data replication, ETL/ELT tools, cloud and software defined infrastructure tools (for instance AWS Cloud Formation, Kubernetes, Docker), API technologies and analytics is definitely a plus

This is a senior, high-impact role for a data engineering generalist who wants to spend their time in public. You will execute developer experience and developer relations work across our product surface — such as dbt State, dbt Fusion, and dbt Wizard, and the Fivetran connector SDK — helping practitioners succeed with our tools and raising our thought leadership in open data infrastructure.

AI is reshaping parts of this landscape and you should be comfortable working with it and curious about where it goes.

This is a highly autonomous role. You will set your own priorities, communicate them clearly, and deliver high-quality work without heavy direction. In exchange you get real ownership of a focus area, significant internal and external visibility, and leadership that protects your time rather than managing your calendar. We're looking for someone who can hit the ground running — shipping meaningful work within their first two weeks.

This is a full-time, fully remote position based in the United States. This role reports to the Director of Community, Developer Experience & AI.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build prototypes, reference implementations, and example repositories that show practitioners how to get real work done with our tools
  • Create working prototypes that validate product direction and accelerate engineering iteration
  • Build tooling that removes friction from common analytics engineering workflows
  • Author technical content for the dbt Developer Blog, guides, and documentation that makes complex concepts actionable for practitioners
  • Publish knowledge and best practices on data and analytics engineering that establish you as a resource in your product area
  • Develop enablement resources for internal teams and the dbt Community, and contribute to product launches as a subject matter expert
  • Represent your product area as a community voice across Community Slack, GitHub, conferences, and public forums
  • Collect and synthesize community feedback, surfacing insights to product and engineering, and bring the practitioner perspective into product design reviews
  • Identify and flag sharp edges, regressions, or gaps in the developer experience
  • Maintain and triage relevant open source repositories and community projects, contributing code and design reviews with an eye toward developer ergonomics

Skills We're Looking For

  • 5+ years in data engineering, analytics engineering, or a closely related field, with strong general knowledge of the data industry and how it is changing
  • Hands-on dbt knowledge and practitioner-level fluency
  • Expert public communication in both spoken and written technical contexts, with a track record of published articles or public-facing content on data or analytics engineering — we will want to read and watch your work
  • Strong data and analytics engineering fundamentals, including comfort with Python and SQL and the ability to contribute to open source codebases
  • Comfort and familiarity with AI, and enthusiasm for adapting AI into how you work
  • Ability to work autonomously as a self-starter, delivering high-quality output with minimal direction, with the operational rigor to set priorities and communicate them clearly at multiple cadences
  • Strong product sense, the ability to translate user needs into concrete product feedback, and genuine enthusiasm for a public-facing role over internal product or engineering work

Bonus Skills

  • An existing footprint in the dbt Community, or prior hands-on use of dbt tools
  • Background in developer relations, developer experience, or developer advocacy at a developer tools company
  • Experience building with or for AI coding agents, and fluency with how the AI agent ecosystem is evolving
  • Contributions to open source projects in the data ecosystem (packages, adapters, community tools)
  • Public speaking experience at data or developer conferences, and experience with Fusion and the dbt platform

In this role, you will learn the data models behind our sales, billing, and customer operations, design how data should be structured to support those processes, and build the transformations and pipelines that move data reliably between our internal systems.

This position sits at the crossroads of data engineering, data modeling, and business process, ensuring our internal data is accurate, well-structured, and ready to scale. You will partner closely with our Systems and Analytics Engineering teams, as well as Sales Operations, Finance, and other business partner teams.

This is a full-time position based out of our Novi Sad, Serbia office.

Technologies You’ll Use
Our core systems are Salesforce, Netsuite, Coupa, Workday, and Zendesk, with Salesforce at the center of our sales and billing data. Our current integration stack includes Celigo and Fivetran itself.

Working knowledge of one or more of our business applications, with a desire to keep learning, is necessary. You should also be fluent in SQL and strong in a general purpose programming language such as Python or Typescript.

A data engineering background is strongly preferred, with proficiency in data modeling, ETL/ELT development, data quality testing, and data validation. Help us bring established data engineering practices to internal business systems!

What You’ll Do

  • Learn the data models behind Fivetran's sales, billing, and product operations, and document how business concepts map to data in our core systems.
  • Design target data models and field mappings when consolidating or migrating data between systems.

  • Define and enforce standards for data quality, data modeling, and governance across internal systems.
  • Validate data before and after migrations and pipeline changes, reconciling record counts, values, and business rules with stakeholders.
  • Build monitoring, alerting, and data quality checks that give end-to-end visibility into data freshness and accuracy.
  • Work with business partner teams to understand their processes and translate requirements into data models and transformations.
  • Investigate and resolve data issues raised by other teams, often requiring root cause analysis across multiple systems.

  • Working knowledge of business applications such as Salesforce, Netsuite, Coupa, Workday, and Zendesk.

Bonus Skills

The dbt Core team are the stewards of the open-source engine that powers the modern data stack for tens of thousands of practitioners. This small, high-trust group of systems engineers tackles the most fundamental challenges in dbt: ensuring the performance, reliability, and architectural integrity of dbt itself. They not only own the core execution engine but also architect the crucial adapter framework that connects dbt to a growing ecosystem of databases and data platforms.

 

As a Staff Software Engineer on the Core & Adapters team, you will be a steward of the performance, reliability, and architectural integrity of dbt. You will tackle ambiguous, open-ended problems and take ownership of critical systems.

  • Dive deep into the dbt-core execution engine, using your systems expertise to identify, debug, and eliminate performance bottlenecks in our Python codebase.

  • Architect and implement improvements to our adapter interface, the crucial layer that connects dbt to a growing ecosystem of databases and data platforms, enabling the community to build more powerful and efficient integrations.

  • Debug complex, system-level issues that span from Linux process management and concurrency models to database query planning and network protocols.

  • Lead technical design discussions and contribute to the long-term architectural roadmap for dbt Core, making key decisions about what, how, and when we build to ensure its scalability and reliability for years to come.

  • Mentor other engineers and review contributions from our vibrant open-source community, upholding our high standards for code quality, testing, and design while fostering a collaborative and inclusive environment.

  • Take strong ownership of our distributed systems, troubleshoot complex production issues, and participate in an on-call rotation to maintain high availability and deliver a resilient platform experience.

We are looking for an engineer with a strong performance and debugging mindset, excellent mental models for complex systems, and a deep curiosity for infrastructure and open-source software.

 

Required Qualifications:

 

  • 6+ years of professional software development experience, with a focus on building and operating backend systems in a production environment.
  • Deep backend engineering experience and proficiency in Python.
  • A systematic, first-principles approach to problem-solving, with comfort navigating and debugging in Linux environments (e.g., understanding process scheduling, memory management, file systems).
  • Solid grasp of database internals, such as query execution engines, storage layers, indexing strategies, and transaction management.
  • Excellent communication skills and a sense of ownership, with the ability to balance technical depth with fast, iterative delivery.

Preferred Qualifications:

 

  • A background in data warehousing, data engineering, or analytics engineering.
  • Professional experience writing production code in Go or Rust.
  • Experience contributing to or maintaining a popular open-source project.
  • Experience building compilers, interpreters, or developer tooling.
  • Familiarity with performance analysis tools like perf or strace.

You will join a small, high-trust team of senior and staff-level engineers who are passionate about building robust, well-crafted, and reliable software. We operate in a remote-first, asynchronous-friendly environment that values deep work, clear written communication, and a high degree of autonomy. description:
From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are coming together with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together we're building the data infrastructure layer that moves, transforms, and adds context to data — from the moment it lands to the point where teams and AI systems depend on it.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we're building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products our customers know and trust. It's a good time to join a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work.

About the Role

Product Finance covers two things: how our products perform, and what they cost to build, run, and support. This role owns the cost and investment side, as the finance partner to the Product and Customer Support organizations.

You'll own the operating expense P&L for both organizations — headcount and hiring plans, vendor and program spend, annual planning, monthly close, and budget-vs-actuals — and work with those leaders on where to spend and what to trade off.

You'll also build our view of product investment at the portfolio level: what we spend behind each product line, what it returns, and what that means for how the roadmap gets funded. That includes bringing cost of revenue and unit economics into the picture, so we can talk about product margin rather than just product spend. This is how we'll decide where to invest and where to pull back.

You'll build our cost-to-serve view as well — support cost by account and segment, and the economics of deflection and AI-assisted support.

Expect close work with Product Managers, Support and Engineering leaders, Pricing, Corporate FP&A, and Accounting, and regular exposure to senior leadership as we scale toward public company readiness.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the finance business partner to Product and Customer Support leadership — own their budgets, partner on spend decisions, and flag risks, trade-offs, and reallocation opportunities early.
  • Own the annual operating plan for both organizations, including headcount and hiring plans, vendor and program spend, and quarterly reforecasts.
  • Own monthly close, accruals, and variance analysis — budget vs. actuals with clear driver explanations and forward-looking implications.
  • Build the portfolio view of product investment: what we spend behind each product line, what it returns, and what that implies for roadmap funding and resource allocation.
  • Bring cost of revenue and product unit economics into that view, working with the teams that own the underlying cost data.
  • Build cost-to-serve analytics — support cost by account and segment, and the economics of deflection and AI-assisted support.
  • Build business cases for new product investments and major roadmap decisions, including the economics of retiring or consolidating products, and provide Pricing with the unit economics behind packaging and monetization changes.
  • Co-own the Product Monthly and Quarterly Financial Reviews with the product top-line lead, so cost and performance are presented together.
  • Improve how this work gets done — better data models, less manual assembly, and AI applied to recurring analysis.

What We're Looking For

  • 4+ years in FP&A, strategic finance, product finance, investment banking, or consulting, including ownership of a model or forecast that others relied on.
  • Experience owning an operating expense budget, or partnering with a non-finance organization on its spend.
  • Strong modeling skills across both driver-based revenue forecasts and operating expense and headcount models.
  • Working knowledge of software and subscription economics — ARR, NRR, ARPA, expansion, gross margin — ideally in a usage-based business.
  • Comfort working directly with large and complex datasets. SQL proficiency strongly preferred.
  • Ability to turn analysis into a clear recommendation and present it to Product, Support, and senior leadership.
  • Interest in how software gets built and what it costs to run.

Nice to Have

  • Product or Engineering finance partnership at a software, data infrastructure, or developer tools company.
  • Hands-on product margin, cost of revenue, or cost-to-serve analysis.
  • Experience supporting a Customer Support, Services, or other cost-to-serve organization.
  • Usage-based pricing, packaging, or monetization modeling.
  • Planning and BI tools (Pigment, Looker, Tableau, Sigma) and lightweight automation in Python or SQL.
  • Experience through a period of rapid scaling or IPO preparation.

About the Role

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Semantic Layer team in Bengaluru. You'll own the health, delivery, and growth of the team behind MetricFlow — building and coaching a group of engineers, setting technical direction in partnership with your leads, and ensuring one of the most important projects in the modern data stack keeps shipping with quality and momentum.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend most of your time growing people, running a healthy delivery process, and shaping strategy — but you'll stay close enough to the code and the architecture to make sound technical calls and earn the trust of a senior engineering team. You'll also be the steward of a public, community-facing open-source project, balancing the needs of internal roadmap and external contributors.

About the team

The Semantic Layer team owns the systems that turn dbt models into trusted, reusable business metrics. At the heart of this is MetricFlow — the open-source semantic engine that powers the dbt Semantic Layer. MetricFlow lets data teams define metrics once in code and consume them consistently across BI tools, notebooks, AI agents, and downstream applications.

This team is the steward of MetricFlow as an open-source project: shipping releases, reviewing community contributions, evolving the query compiler, and ensuring it integrates cleanly with the broader dbt ecosystem. The team works at the intersection of language design, query compilation, and distributed data execution — solving problems that directly shape how thousands of organizations measure their business.

What you'll do

  • Lead, coach, and grow a team of software engineers building MetricFlow — hiring, onboarding, career development, performance management, and day-to-day support.

  • Own delivery for the Semantic Layer team: planning, prioritization, execution, and predictable shipping of high-quality software.

  • Partner with your senior and staff engineers to set technical direction across metric definitions, query compilation, dimensional modeling, and SQL generation for multiple data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and others).

  • Partner with product, design, and developer-relations counterparts to translate customer and community feedback into a clear, well-sequenced roadmap.

  • Drive engineering excellence in performance, reliability, and observability of metric query execution at scale.

  • Foster a culture of design docs, thoughtful code review, and durable engineering — shipping fast without shipping sloppy.

Skills we're looking for

  • Experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, and performance management, with a track record of shipping production systems.

  • A strong engineering foundation — you've built and shipped production software yourself and can engage credibly on architecture and technical tradeoffs with a senior team.

  • Familiarity with the technical domain: SQL fundamentals, how analytical query engines and data warehouses execute queries, and systems that involve parsing, compilation, or transformation (query planners, DSL compilers, type systems, or rule-based engines).

  • Solid grasp of software design principles: clean APIs, modularity, testability, and backwards compatibility — and the judgment to hold a team to them.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication — you can explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineers, product managers, and external community members.

  • Experience leading in a distributed, asynchronous team environment.

Nice to have

  • Experience leading or contributing to a popular open-source project, including managing a community of external contributors.

  • Familiarity with dbt, MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or other semantic-layer technologies.

  • Background in data warehousing internals, query optimization, or analytical SQL dialects.

  • Experience with CI/CD, GitHub Actions, and release engineering for Python libraries.

  • Exposure to building developer-facing APIs, SDKs, or CLIs.

Why join us

  • Impact at scale: Your team's code will run inside the data platforms of tens of thousands of companies, including some of the world's largest enterprises.

  • Open-source ownership: You'll lead the team behind a foundational open-source project — visible, reviewed, and used by the global data community.

title: Roboticist, Robot Foundation Model
description:
About us   

Founded in 2017, Wayve is the leading developer of Embodied AI technology.  Our advanced AI software and foundation models enable vehicles to perceive, understand, and navigate any complex environment, enhancing the usability and safety of automated driving systems.

Our vision is to create autonomy that propels the world forward.  Our intelligent, mapless, and hardware-agnostic AI products are designed for automakers, accelerating the transition from assisted to automated driving. 

In our fast-paced environment big problems ignite us—we embrace uncertainty, leaning into complex challenges to unlock groundbreaking solutions. We aim high and stay humble in our pursuit of excellence, constantly learning and evolving as we pave the way for a smarter, safer future.

At Wayve, your contributions matter.  We value diversity, embrace new perspectives, and foster an inclusive work environment; we back each other to deliver impact.  

Make Wayve the experience that defines your career!  

About the role

We are looking for a Roboticist to join the Multi-Embodiment Generalist Agent (MEGA) team within Wayve Labs as a founding member.

MEGA is building foundation models for general-purpose robots beyond self-driving vehicles. Our focus is on creating intelligent agents that can perceive, reason, move and manipulate the physical world across diverse embodiments, including mobile manipulators, dual-arm platforms and humanoids.

This is a high-impact role with genuine 0→1 ownership. You will have the opportunity to work across the entire robot stack: you will select, build, integrate, and maintain robot hardware; develop the software needed to deploy and test robot policies; and work closely with research teams to shape data collection, model evaluation, and the learning loop. The goal is work on compelling and publishable research, but also to turn it into systems that demonstrate increasingly general, robust and useful behavior in the physical world.

You will collaborate closely with researchers, ML engineers, roboticists and hardware teams to move ambitious ideas rapidly from research hypotheses to large-scale experiments and impressive real-world capabilities.

This is a rare opportunity to help build a general robotics effort from the ground up—combining frontier foundation-model research with the immediacy and complexity of intelligence embodied in real machines.

What you’ll do

  • Build, maintain, and operate robot hardware for research and deployment experiments.
  • Implement and maintain C++ and Python robot software, including control, planning, and ROS/ROS2-based systems.
  • Develop infrastructure for policy deployment, data collection, and the robot learning data flywheel.
  • Run experiments on robots and define data collection pilots that accelerate model development.
  • Debug and troubleshoot robotic software, hardware, and policy failures in lab environments.
  • Build comprehensive deployment and regression tests to improve reliability and repeatability.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience in robot manipulation; working with robot hardware.
  • Experience with C++ and Python in robotics or ML environments.
  • Strong robotics and machine learning fundamentals, with the ability to translate research into robust systems.
  • Publications in top-tier conferences such as ICRA, CoRL, or IROS are highly valued.
  • PhD preferred; MS acceptable with strong relevant experience.

What makes this role exciting

  • Join a new, well-resourced effort at the intersection of foundation models and robotics.
  • Work on generalist robot models and help build the full flywheel around data, architecture, deployment, and evaluation.
  • Work with real robots at serious scale.
  • Own meaningful 0→1 technical scope in a fast-moving research environment.
  • Help define how foundation model research becomes reliable embodied intelligence.

 

This role is a full-time role based in Sunnyvale, CA (hybrid) and the reasonably estimated salary for this role ranges from $184,200 to 240,000, plus a competitive equity package. Actual compensation is based on the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. At Wayve we want the best of all worlds so we operate a hybrid working policy that combines time together in our offices and workshops to fuel innovation, culture, relationships and learning, and time spent working from home. We operate core working hours so you can determine the schedule that works best for you and your team.

 

Wayve is committed to creating an inclusive interview experience. If you require any accommodations or adjustments to participate fully in our interview process, please let us know.

We understand that everyone has a unique set of skills and experiences and that not everyone will meet all of the requirements listed above. If you’re passionate about self-driving cars and think you have what it takes to make a positive impact on the world, we encourage you to apply.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition  (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.  

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. 

To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve 

For US candidates only, please visit E-Verify Notice and Participation and Right to Work

title: Senior Software Engineer - Developer Productivity
description:
From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.
​
During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Sr Software Engineer to join the Platform Ops team (Platform Engineering) and enable developer productivity by building and improving developer tooling and environments, and by improving other productivity tools around observability. Our team builds the shared systems and workflows engineers rely on every day—internal developer environments and self-serve tooling that makes the recommended way to ship changes the easiest way. This is a platform tooling role with a focus is on reusable capabilities and self-service workflows adopted across teams.

You’ll also help develop AI-based workflows for productivity and efficiency, including automation that improves infrastructure operations (for example, faster triage, automated runbook steps, and better self-service for common issues). You’ll prioritize the highest-impact problems by looking at where time is being lost today (slow builds, flaky tests, manual release steps, repetitive operational work) and turning that into concrete projects. You’ll set clear success metrics up front and use them to guide design decisions and rollouts.

Expect to partner closely with engineering teams to drive adoption, document changes, and iterate based on feedback. You’ll drive cross-team work across internal tooling, developer environments, observability, and reliability, focusing on measurable improvements (for example: shorter lead time, fewer incidents, and faster recovery). You’ll add automation and enable developer workflows across all three major cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and GCP).

Over time, you’ll own medium-sized projects end-to-end: identify the highest-friction workflows with partner teams, build and ship improvements, roll them out safely, and iterate based on adoption and measurable outcomes (for example: faster builds, fewer flaky tests, shorter time to debug, and less operational toil). You’ll collaborate closely with Platform Engineering, Release Engineering, Security, and product engineering teams to make improvements that are easy to adopt and maintain.

What You’ll Do

  • Build internal tools and services in Python and/or Go
  • Build tooling for our internal developer platform (self-service workflows, shared patterns, developer-facing interfaces)
  • Add automation and enable developer workflows across all three major cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and GCP)
  • Develop AI-based workflows that improve developer experience and reduce repetitive manual work, including efficiency gains in infrastructure operations
  • Improve developer feedback loops through better observability (metrics/logs/traces), making failures easier to diagnose
  • Automate common engineering workflows (scaffolding, environment setup, releases, operational runbooks)
  • Improve observability for platform services (metrics, logs, traces) to make issues easier to detect and debug
  • Integrate tools into existing workflows (CLI, Slack, GitHub, dashboards) where it reduces time-to-resolution
  • Participate in on-call/incident response as needed and drive follow-up automation to prevent repeat issues

Skills We’re Looking For

  • Professional software engineering experience in Python and/or Go
  • Experience building developer productivity tooling (CI systems, build tooling, developer portals, workflow automation)
  • Experience with at least one cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP)
  • Strong fundamentals: testing, code review, debugging, and operating production services
  • Ability to work effectively in a remote, cross-team environment

You'll have an edge if you have:

  • Kubernetes experience
  • Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/OpenTofu), including reusable modules and safe state management

We're looking for a Marketing Operations Manager on our Marketing Operations team to own lead management and revenue handoff — the routing logic and BDR tooling workflows leads and contacts move through, and the rules that determine how and when marketing hands them to sales.

This role owns the scoring and routing logic that runs on our core marketing and sales platforms, plus a set of adjacent lifecycle processes — MQL definitions, SLA design, lead source governance, ABM list management, and partner-sourced lead triage. You'll partner with our Sr. Marketing Operations & Technology Manager, who owns core platform administration, and with Sales/BDR leadership on the day-to-day handoff relationship.

This is a full-time, fully remote position based in Costa Rica, with working hours aligned to the Central Time zone to support close, real-time collaboration with our Oakland, CA-based team and US sales organization.

  • Marketo, LeanData, Salesforce, Outreach, Nooks, Clay, etc.

Scoring & Routing

  • Build, maintain, and calibrate the lead scoring model in Marketo, using BDR feedback and closed-won/lost data to keep it predictive rather than stale
  • Own lead routing logic and governance in LeanData — match rules, ownership logic, and routing paths — in partnership with the Sr. Marketing Operations & Technology Manager on platform administration
  • Own MQL definitions and the marketing-to-sales handoff process, including SLA design and ongoing SLA monitoring

Lifecycle & Handoff Processes

  • Own lead/contact lifecycle status management and lead source governance
  • Own inbound and partner-sourced lead triage/routing processes
  • Manage ABM account list and signal strategy in partnership with enterprise sales stakeholders
  • Optimize BDR tooling workflows across Outreach, Nooks, and Clay — sequence/cadence logic, data flow between tools, and adoption — within the platform and vendor decisions set by Systems and leadership
  • Set and enforce SFDC data entry standards for sales-owned fields relevant to lead/contact records, in partnership with Sales leadership
  • Run a regular Sales & MOps alignment cadence with sales/BDR leadership to review routing and handoff health

Skills We’re Looking For

  • 4–6 years of experience in marketing operations, revenue operations, or lifecycle roles in B2B SaaS or high-growth environments
  • Direct, hands-on experience building and calibrating lead scoring models in Marketo
  • Experience owning lead routing logic in LeanData or a comparable platform
  • Working knowledge of SQL sufficient to validate routing and scoring outcomes against CRM data
  • Experience partnering with sales or BDR leadership on lead handoff logic, SLAs, routing rules, and CRM data standards
  • Comfortable working independently across US business hours as part of a distributed team
  • Ability to use conversational AI systems (like Claude, ChatGPT, or internal tools) to support researching, documenting, and troubleshooting scoring and routing logic, and to synthesize funnel/handoff diagnostics

(Optional )Bonus Skills​

  • Experience working within BDR-facing tools (Outreach, Nooks, Clay, or comparable) to improve workflow efficiency
  • Experience with Bizible/Marketo Measure, Demandbase, or other ABM platforms
  • Prior experience mentoring or supporting more junior marketing operations team members

title: Lead Technical Program Manager, Data
description:
About us   

Founded in 2017, Wayve is the leading developer of Embodied AI technology.  Our advanced AI software and foundation models enable vehicles to perceive, understand, and navigate any complex environment, enhancing the usability and safety of automated driving systems.

Our vision is to create autonomy that propels the world forward.  Our intelligent, mapless, and hardware-agnostic AI products are designed for automakers, accelerating the transition from assisted to automated driving. 

In our fast-paced environment big problems ignite us—we embrace uncertainty, leaning into complex challenges to unlock groundbreaking solutions. We aim high and stay humble in our pursuit of excellence, constantly learning and evolving as we pave the way for a smarter, safer future.

At Wayve, your contributions matter.  We value diversity, embrace new perspectives, and foster an inclusive work environment; we back each other to deliver impact.  

Make Wayve the experience that defines your career!  

The role

As the Lead Technical Program Manager for Data at Wayve, you'll build and lead the technical program management function for our Data org - the data platform, ingestion, standardisation pipelines, and the enrichment, curation, and labelling that fuel the AI Driver. The data corpus is also critical for teams working on simulation and validation.

You'll be the delivery partner to engineering leadership for data teams and drive the department wide objective to “make valuable data immediately and reliably usable”. You will leading flagship programs yourself while supporting and coaching a small, high-impact TPM team. Your impact is measured in data quality, throughput, cost, and how predictably the data that powers every model lands. A successful TPM leader is a force multiplier - helping teams move faster, more effectively, and with purpose.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the function: Build, coach, and grow a small TPM team; hire to fill gaps and raise the bar.
  • Own data delivery: Partner with Data leadership on planning, prioritisation, and execution across the data roadmap.
  • Trusted partner for Engineering: You are a leader in the org. You will maintain the partnership with Engineering leaders to land big outcomes, pushing teams to land impact with high leverage and hold leaders to account.
  • Drive flagship programs directly: Data platform, data pipelines, enrichment & curation, labelling / annotation, and dataset management and quality.
  • Establish scalable practices: Planning cadences, governance, KPIs and dashboards, escalations and operational reviews.
  • Align cross-functionally: Work with data, ML, engineering, and external data / annotation suppliers; manage dependencies, risk, and trade-offs.
  • Connect to outcomes and represent the data org: Tie delivery to data quality, throughput, cost, and time-to-insight, and represent the data org in company-level reviews.

About you

In order to set you up for success as a Lead Technical Program Manager, Data at Wayve, we're looking for the following skills and experience. (The first four are our must-haves.)

Essential

  • 8+ years in data: Deep, hands-on experience delivering data programs as a technical program manager - data platform, pipelines, enrichment / curation, labelling - including people and process leadership. You've built or scaled a program function and you get things done with ownership and a bias for action.
  • People leadership: You build, coach, and grow high-performing teams, and raise the bar on the craft.
  • Technically strong: Credible with engineers on data platforms, pipelines, and large-scale data infrastructure, even though you won't write production code. Experience with distributed data platforms at Petabyte scale.
    • Experience with data ingestion from raw data to processing through different stages and pipelines. Understands Directed Acyclic Graphs, their usage and challenges.
    • Solid understanding of Machine Learning, GPUs and training and inference of 500M-20B parameter models.
    • Proficient with some or all of Databricks, Flyte, Ray, Kubernetes, Azure, Docker, Python.
    • Proficient with AI Agents to accelerate execution: eg. Cursor, Claude, Codex.
  • Stays neutral and adapts under pressure: Effective in ambiguous, fast-moving environments; you flex your style and bring structure without slowing delivery.
  • Systems thinking: You reason about how the parts of a complex data system fit together, and how a change in one area ripples into others.
  • Product-minded: You focus on outcomes and the people your programs serve - prioritising by impact and defining what good looks like, not just tracking activity.
  • Exceptional cross-functional leadership: You align and influence across data, ML, and engineering without relying on authority.
  • Strategic & business impact: You link data investment to measurable outcomes - quality, throughput, cost.
  • Clear, data-driven communicator: You set direction with clarity and steer with the right metrics.
  • Growth mindset: Open to feedback and always looking to improve.

Desirable

  • Working experience with a large scale distributed data platform used by 100s of engineers and researchers.
  • Background in autonomous vehicles, robotics, or another large-scale data / ML program.
  • An engineering or computer science degree, or experience working as an engineer; fluent with modern delivery tooling (e.g. Jira).

This role is a full-time role based in Sunnyvale, CA (hybrid) and the reasonably estimated salary for this role ranges from $259,200 to $312,400, plus a competitive equity package. Actual compensation is based on the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience.

Wayve is committed to creating an inclusive interview experience. If you require any accommodations or adjustments to participate fully in our interview process, please let us know.

We understand that everyone has a unique set of skills and experiences and that not everyone will meet all of the requirements listed above. If you’re passionate about self-driving cars and think you have what it takes to make a positive impact on the world, we encourage you to apply.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition  (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

description:

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.
​
During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join the Platform Ops team (Platform Engineering) and lead initiatives that enable developer productivity by building and improving developer tooling and environments, and by improving other productivity tools around observability. Our team builds the shared systems and workflows engineers rely on every day—internal developer environments and self-serve tooling that makes the recommended way to ship changes the easiest way.

This is a platform tooling role with a focus is on reusable capabilities and self-service workflows adopted across teams. You’ll also help develop AI-based workflows for productivity and efficiency, including automation that improves infrastructure operations (for example, faster triage, automated runbook steps, and better self-service for common issues). You’ll prioritize the highest-impact problems by looking at where time is being lost today (slow builds, flaky tests, manual release steps, repetitive operational work) and turning that into concrete projects. You’ll set clear success metrics up front and use them to guide design decisions and rollouts. Expect to partner closely with engineering teams to drive adoption, document changes, and iterate based on feedback. You’ll drive cross-team work across internal tooling, developer environments, observability, and reliability, focusing on measurable improvements (for example: shorter lead time, fewer incidents, and faster recovery). You’ll add automation and enable developer workflows across all three major cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and GCP). 

As a staff engineer on the team, you’ll lead medium-to-large initiatives end-to-end: define the problem with stakeholders, write a design and rollout plan, build and operate the solution in Python/Go, and measure results. You’ll work across Platform Engineering, Release Engineering, Security, and product engineering teams to make improvements that are adopted broadly and remain reliable over time.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead end-to-end projects that improve developer tooling, environments, and operational workflows (speed, reliability, and safety)
  • Design and operate internal tooling/services in Python and/or Go
  • Build tooling for our internal developer platform (self-service workflows, shared patterns, developer-facing interfaces)
  • Add automation and enable developer workflows across all three major cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and GCP)
  • Develop AI-based workflows that improve developer experience and reduce repetitive manual work, including efficiency gains in infrastructure operations
  • Improve developer feedback loops through better observability (metrics/logs/traces), making failures easier to diagnose
  • Design/build and document “paved paths” and self-service capabilities so teams can ship without extensive platform expertise
  • Improve reliability through automation and observability (metrics/logs/traces), and drive incident follow-ups to reduce recurrence
  • Set technical direction (design docs, tradeoffs, sequencing) and drive delivery across stakeholders
  • Mentor engineers through design and code reviews

Skills We’re Looking For:

  • Strong experience building and operating production services in Python and/or Go
  • Experience with at least one cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and core primitives (IAM, networking, compute)
  • Experience building developer productivity tooling (CI systems, build tooling, developer portals, workflow automation)
  • Track record leading ambiguous, cross-team technical projects to completion
  • Strong communication and engineering judgment

       You'll have an edge if you have:

  • Kubernetes/platform abstractions experience
  • Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/OpenTofu), including reusable modules, safe state practices, and modernization of shared platform foundations

This is a rare opportunity to work at the intersection of systems programming, database internals, and high-visibility open-source development. Your work will shape a foundational platform leveraged across the dbt ecosystem and the broader data community.

  • Strong programming background in Rust, Go, C++ or similar performance-oriented languages.
  • Experience designing or maintaining SDKs, libraries, connectors, or compute/data integration codebases.
  • Exposure to data warehouses, query engines, Arrow/columnar ecosystems, or execution runtimes.
  • A desire to build foundational platform components that other teams and community members rely on.
  • Comfort working in public code review loops, async-first communication, and collaborative RFC processes.
  • A mindset grounded in debuggability, reliability, and ownership in ambiguous problem spaces.
You’ll have an edge if you have:
  • Contributed to or interacted with Arrow, ADBC, DuckDB, Presto, DataFusion, Spark, ClickHouse, or similar engines.
  • Experience shaping adapter/plugin standards, driver contracts, or architectural interfaces used by others.

  • Prior OSS governance experience — triaging issues, reviewing PRs, or working with community maintainers.
  • An interest in building developer-experience layers or scaffolding frameworks for adapter authors.

About the Role

You'll spend much of your time helping managers tackle the things that make leading people hard: giving clear feedback, addressing performance early, navigating change, building effective teams, and making good decisions when the answer isn't obvious. We don't expect you to have a playbook for everything. We do expect you to be curious, use good judgment, ask the right questions, and be comfortable forming a point of view. We're looking for a People Business Partner to join our Regional HRBP team and support managers across North America. Our Regional HRBP model is new, so you'll also help us build it. You'll work closely with Functional HRBPs and partners across the People team, learning from what you see on the ground and helping us create better, simpler ways of working as we grow. You'll report to the Director, Regional HR Business Partners.

What You’ll Do

  • Coach managers. Help managers work through performance, feedback, development, conflict, team dynamics, and difficult people decisions. The goal isn't to solve everything for them, it's to help them become better managers.
  • Get underneath the problem. What first lands as a performance issue might actually be unclear expectations, a struggling manager, a team dynamic, or something else entirely. You'll ask good questions, understand the context, and help determine what needs to happen next.
  • Handle complex people matters. You'll lead performance and employee relations work across North America, balancing good judgment, employee experience, business needs, consistency, and risk. You'll know what you can handle yourself and when to bring in Legal or another People partner.
  • Help teams perform better. You'll work with managers on team health, engagement, talent, performance, and change using both what you're hearing and what the data tells us.
  • Spot patterns. We don't want to solve the same problem five times without asking why it keeps happening. You'll connect dots across teams, use data where it helps, and bring emerging themes and risks to the right people.
  • Work closely with Functional HRBPs. They'll bring the broader functional and leadership context; you'll bring what you're seeing with managers, employees, and teams across the region. You'll work together without duplicating each other's roles.
  • Help us build. This is a new model and not everything will be perfectly defined on day one. You'll help us figure out what works, challenge what doesn't, and build approaches we can scale.
  • Look for a better way. We're interested in where technology, automation, and AI can remove repetitive work or help us make better decisions. You don't need to be an AI expert—we do want you to be curious and willing to experiment.

Skills We’re Looking For

  • You've worked as a People/HR Business Partner, or in a role where you've coached managers and dealt with meaningful people and team challenges.
  • You have strong working knowledge of US employment practices. Experience supporting employees across multiple US states is strongly preferred; broader North American experience is a plus.
  • You're a strong manager coach. You can be supportive without simply agreeing, and you're comfortable saying the thing that needs to be said.
  • You have good judgment. When something messy lands, you can work out what matters, what the risks are, and what you'd recommend doing.
  • You're agile. Priorities change, organizations change, and sometimes the plan changes. You can adjust quickly and keep moving.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You don't need every process or boundary defined before you can make progress.
  • You're interested in the business behind the people question. You want to understand what a team is trying to accomplish before deciding what good People support looks like.
  • You can work independently without operating in a silo. You know when to make the call, when to ask for another perspective, and when something needs to be escalated.
  • You notice patterns. You're interested not only in solving today's issue but in understanding why it's happening and whether we're seeing it elsewhere.
  • You're comfortable working across teams, functions, and time zones in a distributed company.

Bonus Skills​

You don't need all of these, but we'd be particularly interested if:

  • You enjoy working with data and have used engagement, performance, attrition, workforce, or other People data to investigate a problem or challenge an assumption.
  • You've worked with or are interested in People analytics or visualization tools. You don't need to be an analyst—we care more about whether you're curious enough to ask the next question.
  • You're interested in AI and how it could change the way managers and People teams work.
  • You've helped build or improve something rather than only operating within an established model.
  • You've worked through a merger, integration, rapid growth, or significant organizational change.

description:

With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us


Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on. Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions. As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact. During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

You'll spend much of your time helping managers tackle the things that make leading people hard: giving clear feedback, addressing performance early, navigating change, building effective teams, and making good decisions when the answer isn't obvious. We don't expect you to have a playbook for everything. We do expect you to be curious, use good judgment, ask the right questions, and be comfortable forming a point of view. We're looking for a People Business Partner to join our Regional HRBP team and support managers across North America. Our Regional HRBP model is new, so you'll also help us build it. You'll work closely with Functional HRBPs and partners across the People team, learning from what you see on the ground and helping us create better, simpler ways of working as we grow. You'll report to the Director, Regional HR Business Partners.

What You’ll Do

  • Coach managers. Help managers work through performance, feedback, development, conflict, team dynamics, and difficult people decisions. The goal isn't to solve everything for them, it's to help them become better managers.
  • Get underneath the problem. What first lands as a performance issue might actually be unclear expectations, a struggling manager, a team dynamic, or something else entirely. You'll ask good questions, understand the context, and help determine what needs to happen next.
  • Handle complex people matters. You'll lead performance and employee relations work across North America, balancing good judgment, employee experience, business needs, consistency, and risk. You'll know what you can handle yourself and when to bring in Legal or another People partner.
  • Help teams perform better. You'll work with managers on team health, engagement, talent, performance, and change using both what you're hearing and what the data tells us.
  • Spot patterns. We don't want to solve the same problem five times without asking why it keeps happening. You'll connect dots across teams, use data where it helps, and bring emerging themes and risks to the right people.
  • Work closely with Functional HRBPs. They'll bring the broader functional and leadership context; you'll bring what you're seeing with managers, employees, and teams across the region. You'll work together without duplicating each other's roles.
  • Help us build. This is a new model and not everything will be perfectly defined on day one. You'll help us figure out what works, challenge what doesn't, and build approaches we can scale.
  • Look for a better way. We're interested in where technology, automation, and AI can remove repetitive work or help us make better decisions. You don't need to be an AI expert—we do want you to be curious and willing to experiment.

Skills We’re Looking For

  • You've worked as a People/HR Business Partner, or in a role where you've coached managers and dealt with meaningful people and team challenges.
  • You have strong working knowledge of US employment practices. Experience supporting employees across multiple US states is strongly preferred; broader North American experience is a plus.
  • You're a strong manager coach. You can be supportive without simply agreeing, and you're comfortable saying the thing that needs to be said.
  • You have good judgment. When something messy lands, you can work out what matters, what the risks are, and what you'd recommend doing.
  • You're agile. Priorities change, organizations change, and sometimes the plan changes. You can adjust quickly and keep moving.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You don't need every process or boundary defined before you can make progress.
  • You're interested in the business behind the people question. You want to understand what a team is trying to accomplish before deciding what good People support looks like.
  • You can work independently without operating in a silo. You know when to make the call, when to ask for another perspective, and when something needs to be escalated.
  • You notice patterns. You're interested not only in solving today's issue but in understanding why it's happening and whether we're seeing it elsewhere.
  • You're comfortable working across teams, functions, and time zones in a distributed company.

Bonus Skills​

You don't need all of these, but we'd be particularly interested if:

  • You enjoy working with data and have used engagement, performance, attrition, workforce, or other People data to investigate a problem or challenge an assumption.
  • You've worked with or are interested in People analytics or visualization tools. You don't need to be an analyst—we care more about whether you're curious enough to ask the next question.
  • You're interested in AI and how it could change the way managers and People teams work.
  • You've helped build or improve something rather than only operating within an established model.
  • You've worked through a merger, integration, rapid growth, or significant organizational change.

About the role

We're looking for a Partner Solutions Architect to join Fivetran + dbt Labs and own the technical relationship with our ISV partner ecosystem.

This is a global, product-facing partner role rather than a regional field role. You will be the person who decides — with our product team — what we build with our ISV partners and in what order, and the person who explains the combined dbt + Fivetran product offering to that ecosystem. The ISVs in scope span business intelligence, semantic and metrics consumption, catalog and metadata, governance, observability, activation, and the fast-growing set of AI and agent platforms building against our metadata and MCP surfaces.

Success in this role will require developing a defensible prioritization point of view, a coherent technical narrative, and a repeatable way to enable partner architects and sellers.

Internally, the role sits at the intersection of field engineering, product management, partnerships, and partner marketing. You will work with product managers across both product lines, with the partner development managers who own the commercial ISV relationships, and with regional Partner Solutions Architects who carry ISV motions into their geographies.

This is a full-time, remote-based position in California.

What you'll do

  • Own the prioritization of partner product priorities across the ISV ecosystem for the entire product suite, working in partnership with product management to translate ecosystem demand into a sequenced, defensible roadmap input.
  • build and maintain a single, current view of ISV integration state, gaps, and opportunities across the combined platform — ingestion, transformation, Fusion, the semantic layer, catalog and metadata, open table formats, and agent interfaces.
  • Own the capability and technical messaging of the combined dbt + Fivetran platform to the ISV ecosystem, including reference architectures, integration patterns, and the joint value narrative partners use with their own customers.
  • Serve as the primary technical counterpart to ISV partner solution architect teams, and partner product leaders, and run the technical cadence with our top ISV relationships.
  • Support and help shape workshops, webinars, hands-on labs, and partner marketing events that carry the technical narrative into the ecosystem at scale.
  • Equip ISV partner field teams with the demo narratives, architectures, and use cases they need to position the combined platform accurately.
  • Act as the structured feedback loop from the ISV ecosystem into product and engineering — surfacing integration gaps, friction points, competitive dynamics, and roadmap opportunities with evidence rather than anecdote.
  • Partner with regional Partner Solutions Architects and Partner Development Managers so global ISV strategy translates into regional field execution.
  • Build reusable collateral, playbooks, and enablement assets that let the broader partner solutions architecture team run ISV motions without you in the room.
  • Travel approximately 30% for partner planning sessions, technical workshops, executive meetings, and ecosystem events, including international travel.

What you'll need

  • 5+ years in solutions architecture, sales engineering, partner engineering, technical product management, developer relations, or another customer-facing technical role in data and analytics.
  • Direct experience with ISV, technology partner, or product partnership motions — a track record of shaping what a partner built, not only how it was sold.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence a product roadmap you did not own: gathering requirements, building a prioritization case, and getting it accepted by product leadership.
  • Strong hands-on background in SQL, data modeling, and modern data platform architecture, with genuine technical credibility in front of partner engineers.
  • Fluency across the modern data stack — ingestion, transformation, orchestration, warehouses and lakehouses, open table formats, semantic layers, catalogs, BI, and the emerging agent and MCP layer — and the ability to explain how the pieces fit.
  • Excellent technical writing. A meaningful share of this role's output is documentation partners read without you present.
  • Strong presentation and facilitation skills for workshops, webinars, and large partner technical sessions.
  • Comfort operating globally, and across highly cross-functional internal environments.
  • Proven ability to drive outcomes in ambiguous, fast-moving situations with many stakeholders and no direct authority.

What will make you stand out

  • Experience at or with a data ISV in BI, catalog, governance, observability, activation, or AI tooling.
  • Hands-on experience with dbt and with Fivetran.
  • Experience with partner-facing APIs, SDKs, or integration certification programs.
  • Experience building a partner technical community — office hours, developer advocacy, or champion programs.
  • Background in product management or technical product marketing alongside a field engineering career.
  • Familiarity with cloud marketplace motions and co-sell programs.
  • Experience navigating partnerships where the partner is also a competitor in part of the stack.
  • A track record of building credibility quickly with partner engineers, partner product managers, and internal product teams.

With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.

During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

We're looking for a strategic, results-oriented organic growth lead to drive our acquisition strategy across traditional search engines and emerging AI/LLM platforms. You'll directly shape the vision, strategy, and operating model responsible for driving measurable growth in organic visibility, discoverability, and pipeline through content creation across owned and earned channels. You’ll partner closely with creative, product marketing, web, PR, and brand teams to identify content gaps and build plans, establish investment priorities, and ensure we're positioned to win across an increasingly complex discovery ecosystem. 

Success in this role requires balancing long-term strategic thinking with a willingness to dive deep into execution. You'll establish our long-term strategy and priorities while remaining closely connected to the work — creating and reviewing content, measuring and evaluating performance, and continuously refining how we show up across owned and earned channels.

What You'll Do

  • Own our content-led GEO/SEO strategy, defining the prompts, topics, formats, and ecosystems that drive measurable growth in traffic, visibility, and pipeline
  • Identify and prioritize high-impact content opportunities across product areas, influencing cross-functional teams to bring that content to life
  • Map and optimize our presence across the full ecosystem of LLM-ingested content, including YouTube, Reddit, and review sites, to improve AI-driven discoverability
  • Design and execute a comprehensive off-page strategy, including link acquisition, digital PR, and authority-building initiatives
  • Own technical execution — site architecture, crawlability, structured data, and page performance — partnering with web development teams to ensure content is effectively surfaced, indexed, and performant
  • Build net new and repurposed content workflows, leveraging AI tools to accelerate scale and time to production 
  • Lead the relationship with our agency, setting the brief, holding the work to a high bar, and course-correcting as the search landscape shifts.
  • Evaluate emerging trends in search, AI, content consumption, and digital discovery, translating market shifts into strategic opportunities
  • Track and report on organic performance (both SEO and GEO), translating traffic, visibility, and pipeline data into a clear narrative for leadership

Skills We Are Looking For 

  • A proven track record of growing qualified organic traffic and visibility through content strategy and creation
  • A demonstrated point of view on modern organic growth, with a proven ability to anticipate and capitalize on shifts in search, AI/LLM, and digital discovery
  • Experience creating technical content across multiple platforms and channels (YouTube, social, review sites, etc)
  • Strong technical GEO/SEO fundamentals: site architecture, crawlability and indexation (including access for AI crawlers), structured data and schema markup, Core Web Vitals, and content formatting
  • Analytical mindset and comfortable pulling reports, diagnosing performance shifts, and quantifying opportunities
  • Hands-on experience using GEO/SEO tools such as Conductor and Profound to drive strategy.
  • Hands-on experience managing an agency relationship

Technologies You Will Use

  • Profound and/or Conductor 
  • Semrush
  • Google Search Console 
  • Google Analytics (GA4)
  • Screaming Frog
  • Amplitude
  • Looker

Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies.

You will be the driving force behind transforming our 500+ engineers into “Bionic Engineers" while implementing Virtual Engineer capabilities to achieve 10% productivity gains in FY26 and 20% in FY27.

As the single point of contact for AI initiatives in Engineering, you will orchestrate an engineering-wide transformation that makes AI-driven productivity a core engineering competency. This role requires someone who can navigate the rapidly evolving AI landscape, drive adoption across diverse teams, and deliver measurable business impact.

This is a full-time position based out of our Oakland office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including two days in the office each week to connect and build as a team.

  • Java, Postgres, Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, Kubernetes, Docker, AWS, GCP, CircleCI

  • Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot

Adoption Management & Leadership (40%)

  • Drive Cultural Transformation: Lead the evolution from AI-curious to AI-native engineering practices across all teams

  • Champion Change Management: Convert skeptics into advocates through data-driven demonstrations of value and hands-on enablement

  • Measure & Accelerate Adoption: Establish KPIs, track progress from the current 50% to 100% adoption, and implement interventions to accelerate uptake

  • Build Communities of Practice: Create forums for knowledge sharing, celebrate wins, and foster peer-to-peer learning

Technical Leadership (35%)

  • Tool Evaluation & Selection: Continuously assess emerging AI tools (Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, etc.) and make data-driven recommendations

  • Architecture & Integration: Design technical frameworks for integrating AI tools into existing development workflows and CI/CD pipelines

  • Virtual Engineer Implementation: Lead proof-of-concepts for coding agents in standardized tasks (Lite Connectors via CoIL, code refactoring, test generation)

  • Security & Compliance: Partner with Security and Legal teams to ensure AI tool usage protects IP and meets compliance requirements

  • Technical Standards: Establish best practices, guidelines, and guardrails for AI-assisted development

  • Performance Optimization: Analyze and optimize the technical performance and cost-efficiency of AI tool deployments

  • Innovation Pipeline: Maintain awareness of cutting-edge AI developments and identify opportunities for competitive advantage

Business Leadership (25%)

  • Strategic Planning: Develop and execute the three-phase AI adoption roadmap (Explore & Learn → Enable, Train & Adopt → Core Competency)

  • Budget Management: Oversee $1M+ annual tool budget, optimize spend across 500+ team members, and demonstrate ROI

  • Stakeholder Management: Build relationships with the CEO, Engineering Leadership, Finance, L&D, Legal, and Security teams

  • Business Case Development: Quantify productivity gains, cost savings, and strategic value of AI initiatives

  • Vendor Relations: Negotiate enterprise contracts, manage vendor relationships, and influence product roadmaps

  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Work with Program Managers, Engineering Managers, and other non-IC roles to extend AI benefits

  • Competitive Intelligence: Monitor industry trends and ensure Fivetran maintains a leadership position in AI-augmented engineering

  • Enable Success at Scale: Design and implement adoption playbooks that work across diverse teams with varying technical backgrounds

  • Remove Barriers: Identify and systematically eliminate technical, cultural, and process obstacles to AI adoption

  • Communicate Impact: Regularly present adoption metrics, success stories, and ROI to engineering leadership and executives

Skills We’re Looking For

Technical Expertise

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience with proven expertise across multiple programming languages and paradigms

  • Deep hands-on experience with AI-powered development tools (GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, etc.)

  • Strong understanding of LLMs, prompt engineering, and AI model capabilities/limitations

  • Experience with CI/CD, DevOps practices, and modern software development workflows

  • Track record of evaluating and implementing new technologies at scale

​Leadership Experience

  • Proven ability to drive technical initiatives across large engineering organizations (500+ people)

  • Experience leading without authority and influencing senior technical leaders

  • Track record of successful change management in engineering contexts

  • Demonstrated ability to convert technical innovations into business value

  • Experience presenting to C-level executives and board members

Adoption & Enablement Skills

  • Experience driving tool adoption across diverse technical teams

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to create compelling narratives for different audiences

  • Track record of building training programs and enablement materials

  • Data-driven approach to measuring and improving adoption metrics

  • Patience and empathy when working with skeptics and late adopters

Bonus Skills​

  • Experience with Fivetran's tech stack (Java, Python, C, SQL, Bazel, React)

  • Background in developer productivity, platform engineering, or DevEx roles

  • Experience with virtual agents/coding assistants in production environments

  • Knowledge of AI/ML fundamentals and enterprise AI governance

  • Previous experience in high-growth SaaS companies

About the Role

Fivetran and dbt are building the open data infrastructure that powers AI agents you can trust.

Fivetran is looking for a Staff R&D Software Engineer to join our fast-growing Fivetran AI team. Your data stack was built for humans — but agents are the new primary data consumers, and they have fundamentally different requirements. Agents can’t intuit context; it must be explicitly codified, governed, and traceable.
